entry.trigger_summary: The mechanical system he and William Eckhardt taught the Turtles entered on Donchian channel breakouts: System 1 on 20-day highs/lows, System 2 on 55-day highs/lows. His own earlier pit trading was more discretionary but followed the same trend-with-breakout logic (hence discretion = hybrid).
entry.notes: System 1 also had a rule outside this taxonomy: skip the 20-day breakout if the previous breakout signal would have been a winner (take the 55-day failsafe instead). Position limits capped units in closely correlated markets.

exit.notes: Initial stop at 2N (twice the 20-day ATR-like N) from entry; the effective trailing exit was an opposite Donchian breakout (10-day for System 1, 20-day for System 2), exiting the entire position at once.

risk_per_trade_pct.note: Derivation: the published rules size one unit so that a 1N price move equals about 1% of account equity, and the initial stop is 2N from entry, so one unit risks about 2% of equity. max_drawdown_rule.note: Turtle rules: for each 10% drawdown, trade as if the account were 20% smaller, restoring size as equity recovers.

portfolio_heat_cap.note: Turtle position limits: max 4 units per market, 6 units in closely correlated markets, 12 units total in one direction. Pyramiding added units at 0.5N intervals up to the 4-unit market cap.

risk.notes: All numeric risk rules here are from the published system he taught the Turtles; Dennis never publicly disclosed equivalent parameters for his own earlier discretionary trading.

sizing.notes: N-based (ATR-style) unit sizing so each unit represented roughly equal volatility exposure across markets (Original Turtle Rules).
